parsed.explanation: Combined regime has no general criminalisation or police sweeps, and courts enjoin some orders, but a trans visitor faces documented universal exposures: binary federal passports and entry discrepancy refusal with possible fraud ineligibility, federal facilities barred by birth sex, and this state's birth-certificate school/college facility mandate. National custody reports severe abuse and hormone denial if detained. Local ordinances and hate-crime law provide partial recourse but do not displace federal entry, federal facilities, or custody practice. Severity if outed is high; probability is concentrated at documents, federal/school facilities, and any detention.

entry_documents.exposure: X markers stopped for new passports since Feb 2025, Supreme Court allowed restriction Nov 2025, reported confiscations/blocking and stranding. Entry cable: document discrepancy or doubt about sex requires refusal; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry. Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist. Civil-liberties litigation ongoing; legal-aid passport guidance exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport mismatch can trigger entry refusal, investigation and, if detained, federal custody exposure; national document rule overrides protective state/local ordinances.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopted model with hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Number of trans prisoners stopped being reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Earlier national prison LGBTQ protections rescinded, no documented operative custody remedy. Courts and litigation challenge some national orders, but no sourced remedy for custody reports.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry discrepancy or facility trespass arrest can move visitor into custody where birth-sex placement and care denial are documented; efficient federal enforcement amplifies rather than offsets this.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State Protect All Students Act, effective 25 Feb 2025, requires public and private K-12 and colleges to designate bathrooms, locker/changing/shower and overnight accommodation by birth-certificate sex, students must use matching facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State law has no enforcement mechanism and no criminal penalty; single-occupancy controlled restrooms exempt. No general state public-bathroom ban documented. Private facilities and 33 local ordinances may be protective where applicable.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor not enrolled is less exposed to school rule, but federal facilities apply nationally and a travelling minor enrolled/visiting a school could be classified by birth certificate despite local protections.

care_services.exposure: National orders target gender-affirming care for minors and 28 Jan 2025 order frames it as mutilation; this state's care/sports bill bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery under 18. Custody hormone removal documented. Emergency ward placement not documented.
care_services.protection: State care/sports bill blocked Apr 2024, allowed Aug 2024, re-enjoined 18 Mar 2025 with national appeal; operative status unresolved. Several national orders blocked/enjoined. No documented visitor emergency-care exclusion.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitor medication and emergency care are not documented as barred, but detention can interrupt hormones; minor visitor care access depends on unresolved litigation and which provision is enforceable at travel time.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders define sex as binary at birth, remove gender-identity materials and pronoun policies, direct investigation of schools for gender ideology and prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition. Counterterrorism documents use 'radical gender ideology' and 'radically pro-transgender' framing, though not as reward criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No documented trans-presentation offence, police sweeps, extortion campaign or systematic arrest pattern in this state. First known bathroom trespass arrest cited is another state's law, requiring willful entry plus refusal to depart.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing by officials raises outing and confrontation risk, but documented enforcement against adult visitors is concentrated in documents, facilities and custody rather than street sweeps.

minors_guardians.exposure: State school facility law requires birth-certificate facilities and overnight accommodation in K-12/colleges. Jan 2025 law requires staff to out LGBTQ students to parents. Care and sports bans for under-18s are in this bill, operative status unresolved after re-enjoinment. National order targets teachers facilitating transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Facility law has no enforcement mechanism; single-occupancy exemption exists. Care/sports bill currently re-enjoined per last sourced ruling, appeal pending. Trans visitor can marry/recognise same-sex marriage in state since 2015.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult travelling with a minor faces school-related exposure only if minor uses covered schools/colleges or seeks care; guardian does not override birth-certificate or care rules. Parent could be investigated through school/child-document interactions if discrepancy arises.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of trans-specific street violence, police refusal, or organised targeting in this state. National poll 2025: 66% support assigned sex on documents. National hate-crime statistics show sexual-orientation bias is 1/7 to 1/5 of single-bias incidents, not a trans visitor prevalence rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; national employment ruling prohibits gender-identity discrimination. State executive order bars it in state employment since 2018; 33 cities/counties bar it in employment, housing and public accommodations. No state private-sector statute documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Functioning courts/police may prosecute some assaults, but only 23 states cover gender identity in state bias statutes and local ordinance coverage is patchy; recourse does not cure federal document/facility exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport, executive-order and health-rule litigation unresolved; several orders blocked/enjoined, so exposure depends on date of travel. Hospital ward placement, school application in practice, complaints procedures, motor-vehicle Aug 2026 marker rule final text, and county birth-certificate refusals are not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, injunctions against care/sports bill, district-court birth-certificate correction ruling, and local ordinances show courts can provide relief. July 2026 assessment places state second-highest tier, one below four highest-risk jurisdictions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are real but inconsistent and slow for a short-stay visitor; they do not pre-empt federal entry screening, federal facilities or federal custody, and unknown ward/custody placement cannot be treated as safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal birth-sex facility rule and document checking, but this state's general public facilities are not banned, its school law has no enforcement mechanism, and courts enjoin some national measures. Entry and federal custody exposures keep it below 0.55 and near this anchor.

Closest: a birth-sex facility regime upheld without effective access remedy, polite private sector and one prosecuted assault, no presentation offence. Here federal facilities plus passport/entry and custody reports broaden exposure, while school-only state scope and no enforcement narrow it, placing rating around this level.

Higher than this anchor because 0.55 has no general facility ban and courts secure some corrections. Here binary federal passports, entry refusal/fraud risk, federal facility exclusion and documented custody abuse are universal or severe exposures not shown to be corrected.

Lower than 0.65: that anchor has established acceptance, accepted foreign documents, dead-letter sexuality law and court compensation. Here documented social acceptance of trans visitors is not established, documents are restricted, and custody abuse is reported.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document discrepancy at entry or in a federal/school facility leading to refusal, investigation or detention, where birth-sex facilities and documented custody hormone denial/abuse apply. State school law is weaker (no penalty) and courts/local ordinances provide some recourse, preventing a high-risk 0.25-0.35 rating. But national binary documents, federal facility ban, entry fraud risk and severe custody reports are unremedied universal/severe exposures, preventing reduced-risk 0.55+. Hence elevated risk around 0.44.
